title: Excel Changed My 16-Digit Number! Here's the Fix #Shorts
description: Illustrative synthetic sample: Microsoft documents Excel's 15-digit numeric precision limit. Format or import identifiers as Text BEFORE entering them. Existing lost digits cannot be recovered by changing format. Official Microsoft help: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/keeping-leading-zeros-and-large-numbers #Excel #SpreadsheetTips #DataQuality #Shorts Additional official detail: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/format-numbers-as-text

scenes.title: EXCEL CHANGED IT
scenes.narration: A made-up sixteen-digit code ends in six. As an Excel number, its last digit can become zero.

scenes.title: WHY IT HAPPENS
scenes.narration: Excel stores only fifteen significant digits in numeric cells. This isn't just a display issue.

scenes.title: FIX BEFORE PASTE
scenes.narration: Set the column to Text BEFORE you type or paste long identifiers. You can also import as Text.

scenes.title: ALREADY CHANGED?
scenes.narration: Changing cell formatting afterward cannot restore digits Excel already discarded. Return to the original source.

scenes.title: TRY THIS CHECK
scenes.narration: Compare a long code against its source before trusting the spreadsheet. Which digit changed?
